content.intro: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. In this lesson, focus on what frameworks provide; then compare it with framework conventions. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use introduction to php frameworks when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. For introduction to php frameworks, begin with what frameworks provide. Also distinguish framework conventions; routing and middleware; dependency injection. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Introduction to PHP Frameworks
content_blocks.code:
<?php
interface Notifier { public function send(string $message): string; }
final class LogNotifier implements Notifier { public function send(string $message): string { return "logged: " . $message; } }
echo (new LogNotifier())->send("ready") . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
